history.contentIn: Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) depend on sea ice as a platform for hunting seals. Arctic sea ice has declined in extent and thickness over the satellite era as the Arctic has warmed about twice as fast as the global mean (Arctic amplification). The IUCN and Arctic scientists treat loss of sea-ice hunting habitat as the primary long-term threat to the species. Some subpopulations have been relatively stable or better counted in recent surveys, which deniers sometimes quote as 'polar bears are fine.' That snapshot does not cancel the physical dependence on ice or projections of increased fasting and reduced cub survival as ice-free seasons lengthen, especially in southern parts of the range.
